page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based server instance belonging to the Epsv6 family, powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing connection to external high-performance storage volumes.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier ratings in memory bandwidth, reaching 436.06 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 184.19 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Passmark database operations and memory scores also rank in the top tier. Multi-core processing is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 66283.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19664.0. However, single-core execution and large LLM prompt processing are relatively average, showing a clear tradeoff where parallelized workloads and memory-bound tasks are prioritized over raw single-threaded speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers high resource density and exceptional memory bandwidth per unit of compute without the premium cost of traditional x86 memory-optimized hardware. This makes the E32ps_v6 highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. It is less suited for workloads requiring local NVMe storage, heavy single-threaded execution, or GPU-accelerated machine learning.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized server instance from the Epsv6 family, featuring 32 dedicated physical cores on a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. Equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, it provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. While it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, it supports Premium Storage. Benchmarks reveal top-tier memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 436.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 184.19 GB/sec, alongside strong multi-core performance. Conversely, single-core execution and large LLM inference tasks show average to poor results. This hardware profile offers excellent qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads, making it highly suitable for database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
